industry.why: Neutral. Component 1 regime (rates-led late cycle: Richard's view 16-Sep-26, rates and yields rising, inflation high, consumer confidence low, downside skew; sources absent): regulated, leveraged, long-duration assets are hit by his discount-rate line, offset by defensive demand; Ports lead at A but that is leadership only. Relative strength C now, C prior. No tilt.

sector.why: Underweight, set deliberately this week (carried D from the old Telecoms towers row). Component 1 regime, 16-Oct-26 (a discount-rate shock with the first credit crack inside the artificial intelligence chain: United States core inflation re-accelerating on energy, the Fed and Bank of England hikes pulled forward, the US 10-year about 5.1%, the US joined the sell-off and Asia is in washout, defensives bid for four weeks in Europe, European breadth off its three-year lows but in the bottom quarter, the consumer forecast to weaken into winter; sources present 2026-W42): towers are valued off a yield and financed with leverage, the pure long-duration bond proxy, and the discount rate rose again with the hiking path pulled forward. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-16 against 2026-08-14, not week on week: D now, F prior. One live holding, Helios Towers (5.17%, the largest position), whose own case is scored by the Investment Analyst (Bottom-up composite B) and whose Thematic Fit/Momentum reads D through this row; the row is a blunt instrument on it and that is said in component 4. Counter-case: contracted, inflation-linked revenue is the 'visible cash' the regime pays for, and towers rally hardest when rates peak; back to C if the Fed path is marked down.

geography.why: Underweight, carried unchanged with the reason strengthened. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the spillover from France to Italy is the new fact this week (Goldman, 16 Oct, 'tentative spillover to Italy'), and the Italian listings in the Pool are bank-heavy (Monte dei Paschi, Credito Emiliano, Mediobanca) beside global businesses (Eni, Saipem, Tenaris, STMicroelectronics, Technoprobe, Reply). Not Double Underweight because Goldman also says contagion risk is lower than in 2011-15, its fragmentation index shows risk 'remains limited', and Southern European banks are healthier; relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to F if the fragmentation index rises or the Italian premium is read above 150 basis points; back to C under 100.
